business_scope.primary_industry_name: AAA Game Asset 3D Sculpting and Character Rigging Studio

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa - International Company regime administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (unitary national statutory regime with customary law overtones)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus) regional trade agreement
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) in force with Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and the Nordic countries (Denmark, Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden)
No comprehensive double taxation agreement or bilateral investment treaty in force between Samoa and the People's Republic of China

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended), establishing the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) within the Central Bank of Samoa; International Companies Act 1987 (as amended, including the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2021) requiring the registered agent to maintain a beneficial ownership register; International Companies (Fees) Regulations 1998 (Schedule of Fees); FATF 40 Recommendations adopted as the national AML/CFT standard. The beneficial ownership register is kept by the licensed registered agent in Apia and is not publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each shareholder's passport (natural person UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public Office in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention): PRC notary -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> Embassy of Samoa in Beijing -> SIFA/registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Incumbency (if the shareholder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Market Administration for Regulation / Companies Registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (issuing registry or notary -> competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> Samoa Embassy) or, for common-law origin documents, a certified copy chain per the registered agent's KYC manual

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Chinese-language Articles of Incorporation (Constitution) with certified English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed translation firm and PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in PRC -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> Embassy of Samoa in Beijing -> filing with the registered agent and SIFA

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of residential or business address for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the PRC (or other account jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and consular legalization in the country of issue, then forwarding to the Samoan registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse screening of all UBOs, directors and executive officers against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and consolidated sanctions lists, (iii) the Samoa FIU list, and (iv) domestic and adverse-media checks. Politically exposed persons (FATF definition), their family members and close associates require senior compliance officer approval, source-of-wealth documentation and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any positive hit must be escalated immediately to the registered agent's AML compliance officer and, when threshold indicators are met, a Suspicious Transaction Report is filed with the Samoa FIU within statutory timelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) e-Registry - online name reservation module at https://www.sifa.gov.ws
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in the Latin (Roman) alphabet; Chinese characters are not accepted in the legal name. The name must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or the abbreviations 'Ltd', 'Corp', 'Inc', or 'Societe Anonyme' (SA), and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name on the Samoa registers. The Articles of Incorporation (Constitution) may be submitted in Chinese with a certified English translation filed with the registered agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A cleared name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days from the date of SIFA clearance. If rejection occurs, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies at SIFA within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds and any proposed variation. The Registrar must issue a decision within 14 further business days. An unsuccessful administrative appeal may be challenged by judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa. Extension of a reserved name is available by filing a renewal application and paying the prescribed renewal fee before the expiry of the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the statutory seat: every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the office of its licensed registered agent. The 3D game art studio's day-to-day creative operations and workforce may be based abroad (e.g., PRC) as an outsourced back office, provided statutory books, client records, and service-of-process facilities remain with the Apia registered agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - quantified risk approximately 5% per annum for a low-risk standard creative BPO industry. Unannounced physical inspections are not routine, but SIFA and the registered agent may inspect client files and registered office records for AML/CFT compliance, usually with reasonable notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; ss. 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 26
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form 1) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the International Company must issue at least one share, and share consideration is determined by the board without a prescribed minimum deposit
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the International Company adopts its Memorandum and Articles of Association and accepts the subscription for the shares set out in the incorporation documents.
RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent of the Company be the address tendered to the Registrar of International Companies and maintained in Samoa.
RESOLVED, that the first directors named in the statement are appointed, and the secretary named therein holds office until successors are elected.
RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, engage professional advisers, and take all actions needed for registrations, permits and tax exemptions necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa acting for the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a licensed registered agent, instruct a name availability search, and submit Form 1 with two preferred names. The registered agent forwards the reservation request to the Registrar and obtains a name reservation notice for a limited period.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Reservation of Name
Certified copy of proposed subscriber's passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable, file the alternate name reservation immediately; if the name is rejected as prohibited or misleading, submit a new name request without restarting the full incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Proposed subscriber and first directors; counter-signed by licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in English, state the authorized share capital and share classes, identify first directors and secretary, and execute the documents by the subscriber before a witness. The registered agent verifies the signatures and prepares the incorporation submission.
required_dossiers: Statement of first directors and company secretary
Certified passport copies and proof of residence of subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries wording or omissions, the board passes a corrective written resolution and executes replacement memorandum/articles for resubmission within the issued reply period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the complete application package, pays the prescribed government incorporation fee, and awaits issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. The application must include the consent of the registered agent and the address of the registered office in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notice of registered office and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a compliance query, the applicant cures the deficiencies within the stated period; if the application is refused, an appeal may be made to the Supreme Court of Samoa under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Collect Certificate of Incorporation and Establish Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies; company secretary and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, collect the Certificate of Incorporation and certified versions of the Memorandum and Articles. Instruct the registered agent to open the statutory registers, issue share certificates to the initial subscriber, and arrange any required apostille for overseas banking use.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains an error, apply for rectification to the Registrar; if statutory records are incomplete, require the registered agent to deliver corrected registers and share certificates without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Approve Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting or obtain a unanimous written resolution to approve share subscriptions, adopt the registered office and registered agent, confirm first directors and company secretary, approve a bank mandate, and authorize commencement of business.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
Consent to act as company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be reached, the board signs a unanimous written resolution; if a director is unwilling or disqualified, a replacement director is appointed by written board consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Complete Local Administrative Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved commercial bank in Samoa; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour; Ministry of Revenue if local employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation documents, bank mandate resolution, and beneficial ownership declaration with the chosen bank. If the company will have employees, register as an employer with the Ministry of Revenue and obtain the required payroll and taxpayer identifiers. Secure the physical office address and complete any local business notification requirements.
required_dossiers: Board resolution approving bank account opening
Certified passport and proof of address of beneficial owner
Lease agreement or registered office physical address
Employer registration form and payroll account questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide an updated beneficial ownership chain and source of funds statement; if the Ministry of Revenue queries the registration, correct the form and pay any applicable administrative charge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; no industrial licensing board for non-manufacturing creative IT office activities in Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempted; no sectoral operating or manufacturing license required for a 3D game art outsourcing studio operating as an office-based service company

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-level / low-impact exemption: full EIA report not required for an office-based, non-process, non-manufacturing studio
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission process; domestic sewage must comply with municipal sewerage trade waste limits; electronic waste from workstations must be stored, labeled and collected by a licensed recycler; small hazardous waste volumes such as toner and spent batteries are governed by Samoa waste management regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority for office occupancy; building occupancy and structural safety confirmation under Samoa building codes; workplace health and safety inspection covering workstations, electrical installations, emergency exits and fire suppression equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa — national online portal: https://mfr.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned entities must first incorporate as an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). The IC then applies to the Ministry for Revenue for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using the prescribed TIN application form (Form MfR 1), accompanied by the certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, register of directors and shareholders, and a declaration of offshore-only business. TINs are issued within one to two working days. If the IC later obtains a domestic business licence, it must also register for VAGST under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2008 and for PAYE employer obligations before remunerating local staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — a non-resident International Company carrying on exclusively offshore business is exempt from Samoan income tax (initial 20-year exemption, renewable by Ministerial order), exempt from stamp duty, and outside Samoa's territorial tax net; it is not liable to VAGST on offshore turnover. Breach of the offshore-only restriction voids the exemption and reclassifies the entity as a fully taxable Samoan resident.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a US-style check-the-box or LLC pass-through election. Available statutory elections are: (i) an IC may elect to be treated as tax-resident in Samoa if central management and control is exercised there, thereby opting into the normal Income Tax Act 2019 regime; (ii) application to the Minister for Finance to extend or confirm the 20-year tax exemption certificate; (iii) voluntary VAGST registration election; (iv) no hybrid mismatch election is recognised for ICs — the Income Tax Act 2019 general anti-avoidance rules and arm's length principles apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2008
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT$ 100,000 annual taxable turnover (compulsory registration); an offshore-only International Company is not carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa and is therefore not registrable, unless it elects voluntary registration or holds a domestic business licence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no digital stamping requirement, and no government API pre-validation of invoices. VAGST-registered persons must issue tax invoices containing the prescribed particulars under the VAGST Act 2008 and retain duplicate copies, in paper or electronic form, for the seven-year audit window. Electronic invoices generated by MfR-approved accounting systems are acceptable as tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated where the goods are exported in accordance with the VAGST Act 2008 and evidence is furnished within the time prescribed by the Commissioner of Revenue. Offshore services qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-resident, the services are not supplied in connection with land or goods in Samoa, and the services are performed wholly outside Samoa. An International Company supplying 3D game art sculpting and character rigging BPO services to overseas game studios satisfies the export-of-services test; where the IC remains wholly offshore, such turnover is outside the scope of VAGST entirely rather than zero-rated, and any input VAT on local overheads can be recovered only if the IC has elected VAGST registration and makes zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Service Export Declaration / customs clearance documents
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports; for digital 3D art deliverables, electronic delivery evidence, service contract, and milestone acceptance records are substituted
VAGST export certificate / zero-rating claim form endorsed by the Ministry for Revenue
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
International Company certificate of incorporation and tax exemption certificate proving offshore-only status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit for a seven-year period. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims or undeclared domestic activity expose the IC to retrospective VAGST and income tax assessments, penalty tax of 100% to 200% of the tax shortfall, late-payment interest and penalties under the Tax Administration Act (including a 20% per annum penalty rate), criminal fines up to SAT$ 100,000, imprisonment of up to five years for directors, revocation of the International Company tax exemption certificate, and striking-off by the Registrar of International Companies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa is an International Monetary Fund Article VIII member, undertaking current account convertibility for the Samoan tala (WST). Current account payments, including trade in services and profit remittances, are generally permitted through authorised dealers without prior CBS approval, provided the transaction is supported by valid contracts, invoices, and tax clearance where applicable. Capital account transactions, particularly inbound equity injections to local resident companies and offshore lending, remain subject to CBS approval or notification under the Exchange Control Act 1979 and the CBS Exchange Control Guidelines. For an International Company (IC) licensed under the International Companies Act 1988, the exchange control regime is substantially relaxed: the IC is treated as a non-resident offshore vehicle and may maintain foreign currency accounts with authorised dealers without WST conversion requirements. Dividend and profit distributions by an IC to non-resident shareholders are not subject to Samoan tax or exchange control restrictions, provided the IC does not carry on business with Samoan residents and does not hold Samoan-situs property. Practical remittance hurdles arise only where bank compliance requires proof that the IC is not engaged in domestic prohibited activities and that its underlying revenue is sourced from bona fide offshore clients.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident trading entities, export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa through an authorised dealer within 90 days from the date of export, and any proceeds not required for approved foreign exchange obligations must be converted into WST at the prevailing market rate. Mandatory conversion rates for resident exporters are assessed by CBS on a case-by-case basis, generally requiring conversion of 100% of export receipts within the repatriation window unless prior CBS approval has been obtained for retention in a foreign currency account or for direct settlement of offshore liabilities. International Companies are exempt from these surrender rules provided they are not engaged in 'ordinary business' with Samoan residents and do not operate a Samoan domestic business; their export or service receipts may be retained abroad or held in authorised dealer foreign currency accounts in Samoa without mandatory conversion. All exceptions must be supported by a CBS Exchange Control form, the IC's certificate of incorporation, and an annual declaration of non-resident status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not maintain a standalone e-money institution (EMI) or digital payment institution licence. Offshore digital EMIs and payment service providers cannot open bank accounts in Samoa or obtain CBS licensing without establishing a physical branch and complying with the Financial Institutions Act 1996 and the CBS Fit and Proper Guideline. A Samoa International Company may use an offshore EMI for collection of client payments as an auxiliary channel, but this creates significant AML risk because EMI transaction trails are frequently rejected by Samoa banks as insufficient evidence of 'clear source of funds'. The IC is advised to route the majority of inbound revenue through a correspondent-capable commercial bank in Samoa or through a reputable international bank in a low-risk jurisdiction, with the Samoa bank account maintained for formal settlement and operating expenses. PayPal and other digital wallets are permitted as marginal collection tools only where the wallet is held in the IC's name, the wallet history is fully reconcilable to invoices, and the aggregate monthly volume through such channels is kept below USD 5,000 to preserve the Low_Risk_Standard AML rating.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an International Company with non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), all major Samoa banks mandate an in-person or synchronous video KYC interview for each director and UBO, accompanied by certified passport copies and proof of residential address. Physical attendance at a bank branch in Apia is generally required at the initial onboarding stage for signatories of the company's account; however, on a case-by-case basis, ANZ and BSP accept remote opening subject to (i) a notarised corporate resolution, (ii) JP/notary-certified identification, (iii) live video verification by the bank's compliance officer, and (iv) a letter of reference from the IC's registered agent in Samoa. A director's physical presence is strongly recommended when the IC has no prior relationship with the bank, where any UBO is deemed politically exposed, or where the source of wealth originates from digital-asset or high-volume gaming-art transactions. The IC must maintain a current registered agent in Samoa with a physical street address for service of process and bank correspondence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company incorporated in Samoa with no local employees, no local physical premises, and no Samoan directors; bank requires proof of 'substance' and non-resident status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation of the International Company; memorandum and articles of association; registered agent certificate confirming principal place of business and registered office; current Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar of International Companies; sworn declaration of non-resident status; organisational chart showing the headquarters, outsourced 3D art teams, and client relationship management in the studio's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity inbound wire transfers from overseas gaming and entertainment clients without consistent invoice narration may appear as 'unexplained trading activity'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service agreements and master outsourcing agreements; itemised monthly invoices matching the exact wire reference numbers; approved work orders for 3D sculpting and rigging milestones; engine delivery logs and asset-handoff certificates; bank statements and detailed ledgers showing the corresponding accounting entries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal and digital wallet receipts are viewed by banks as high-risk due to chargebacks, third-party funding, and the absence of SWIFT metadata; may trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal business account registration in the IC's name; full exportable PayPal history aligning with client invoices; confirmation of Chinese/regional client KYC from PayPal business verification; chargeback history showing zero or de minimis disputes; a written AML policy and an internal reconciliation procedure for wallet-to-bank sweeps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows to non-resident freelance 3D artists and riggers in multiple jurisdictions trigger 'red flags' on money laundering or unlicensed money remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent contractor agreements with each artist/rigger; task-based invoices and proof of delivery; portfolio evidence and work samples for each milestone; tax identification numbers of contractors; evidence of arm's-length compensation and bank details pre-verified by the company; payroll journal and payment batch files with SWIFT acknowledgements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A Samoa International Company engaged in the active business of creative game art outsourcing may be challenged as 'carrying on business in Samoa' and thus subject to tax or domestic-company reclassification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed description of the off-shore operating model showing all productive activity performed outside Samoa; all client contracts explicitly excluding Samoan-domestic market and Samoan residents; server and communication logs demonstrating offshore management; CBS and Ministry of Revenue declarations; tax exemption certificate under International Companies Act 1988 (if obtained); accountant's confirmation that no Samoan source revenue exists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for the International Company must be routed through the Samoan banking system using SWIFT MT103 messages with a wire purpose code corresponding to 'Business Services' or 'Management & Consulting Fees', e.g., BPM6 service code 'SO' (other business services) or a CBS-compatible narrative and, where required, a CBS Exchange Control Declaration. The corporate bank should be instructed to quote the IC reference number and the inbound remitter's full corporate name and contract reference. The bank will require a certified copy of the shareholder resolution authorising the capital injection and, if structured as a shareholder loan, a written loan agreement with commercial interest rate, repayment schedule, and a statement that Samoa-source income is not used to service the debt. For the game art BPO studio, all inbound client payments should be named strictly as 'Advance for 3D art outsourcing services under Contract [ID]'; any broad descriptions such as 'general funds' or 'investment remittance' will trigger EDD and possible return of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements to overseas 3D artists, rigging freelancers, software licensing vendors, and cloud platform providers must clear through the Samoan correspondent banking network using SWIFT MT103, with full structured remittance information (beneficiary name, account number, BIC, and invoice references). For larger fixed-price production milestones, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit at sight (SWIFT MT700) may be opened through ANZ or BSP, especially where the receiving party requires bank payment undertaking before delivery of high-value character assets. The IC should maintain a multi-currency bank account to reduce conversion spreads and enable direct USD settlement to US-based platform vendors and EU/APAC contractors, thereby avoiding unnecessary WST conversion. All outbound transactions above USD 20,000 should be supported by a payment instruction pack containing: the contract, signed work-order acceptance, milestone sign-off, invoice, and a copy of the receiving artist's/entity's KYC profile held on file. For USD-denominated payroll runs to individual contractors, the bank may require a 'standing instruction' with a cap and pattern of gratitude; deviations from the declared payment pattern must be pre-cleared with the bank's transaction monitoring unit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign exchange forwards (USD/WST) traded with ANZ Bank Samoa Limited and Bank of South Pacific under ISDA terms for up to 3 months tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged offshore in USD against WST basket reference, subject to CBS approval and with the Samoa IC as a non-resident dealer counterparty
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between USD and WST entered through an approved licensed bank for any long-term project finance or capital lease liabilities
FX options and commodity/forward contracts permitted under the CBS's 'Approved Hedge Programs' only for a principal exposure demonstrated from underlying service contracts
Currency swaps via authorised dealer banks to match future milestone receivables in USD with contractor payables in CNY, KRW, KZT, and BRL, provided no resident Samoan counterparty is involved

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Government License Fee Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary date of incorporation; a 30-day administrative grace period is generally recognized before late penalty accrues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the annual fee for non-payment after 30 days; continued non-payment beyond 3 months from the anniversary date may result in administrative strike-off and forfeiture of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Agent and Principal Address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Samoa Registered Agent (submits confirmation to Registrar of International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual government fee, by the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent subjects the company to license suspension and eventual strike-off under the International Companies Act 1987

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a standard International Company under the International Companies Act 1987. An independent audit is mandatory only if the company carries on licensed banking, insurance, or asset-management activities, or if the Registrar issues an audit direction for cause.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with IFRS or an equivalent recognized standard as permitted under the International Companies Act and Samoa corporate practice; no local GAAP audit mandate applies to a standard international company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An International Company must maintain a register of members, register of directors, register of charges, and minute book at its registered office. Samoa does not require a separate public annual UBO filing, but the licensed resident agent must annually confirm and document in its AML/CFT file the identity and ownership percentage of each ultimate beneficial owner. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members promptly, with the UBO register updated and certified to the agent within 14 days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 - $8,000 (only if audit trigger arises; not required for standard exempt company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act 2007 are exempt from Samoan income tax in respect of all income derived from sources outside Samoa; no tax is levied on the shares, debentures, or other securities of an IC, and no estate, gift, or capital gains tax applies to transfers of IC shares. Qualifying enterprises may additionally obtain investment incentives under the Promotion of Investment Act 2018, including a 10-year tax holiday and customs duty concessions for approved pioneer activities. Where the IC holds no Samoan-source income, the effective corporate tax rate is nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 6 — Annual Return of an International Company, filed via the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) Online eRegistry and Company Annual Return Service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 6 months of the end of the IC's financial year (by 30 June for the default calendar-year basis). The prescribed annual government license fee must be settled on the anniversary of incorporation; arrears accrue monthly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC registration number and exact legal name as recorded on the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SIFSA registration number exactly as printed on the certificate; any name variation may nullify the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and the name of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must appoint and retain a Samoa-licensed registered agent; PO boxes alone are not accepted as a registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Particulars of all directors, officers, and the resident secretary (if any).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Samoa IC law permits wholly non-resident boards; no Samoan resident director is required for a standard IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activities description (SIC/ISIC code and narrative).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 7490 — AAA game asset 3D sculpting, character rigging, and creative-game-art outsourcing services rendered to foreign video-game studios.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the registered agent confirming that the IC is not carrying on business in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration is the operative token of the offshore tax exemption; if the agent cannot certify it, the IC loses exemption from Samoan income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual fee schedule declaration (authorized capital band).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual government fee ranges from WS$350 to WS$2,000 per the SIFSA sliding scale based on authorized capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IC annual return attracts a WS$1,000 late-filing penalty plus WS$50 per month of continued default; failure to pay the annual license fee for more than 6 months results in automatic strike-off from the International Companies Register, and the Registrar may forfeit the IC's assets to the Crown without requiring a further court order.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR2 — Company Annual Income Tax Return, submitted through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MoR) SIGTAS e-filing portal (TIN online services) together with underlying financial statements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR2 is due no later than 6 months after the close of the company's year of income (the default year of income is the calendar year; a substituted balance date may be adopted with MoR approval). Any assessed corporate tax is payable on the same due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 9-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC must first obtain a Samoan TIN through the MoR registration workflow, using the registered agent address for correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, and postal contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Samoan registered agent's address as the registered office; foreign correspondence addresses may be disclosed as secondary contact only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of income covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the first SIFSA annual return covered a short period, reconcile the IR2 period to the same period to avoid duplicate declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income: total revenue from all business activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-sourced 3D art outsourcing fees are not Samoan gross income and are generally excluded; include them only in memorandum schedules if the MoR requests global income disclosure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income from sources within Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave at nil unless assets were physically used or services physically performed within Samoa; zero-entry for worldwide pass-through revenue of the tax-exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions incurred in deriving assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct foreign expenses against nil assessable income; excessive expense claims could inadvertently create an allocation of Samoan-source profit through global-apportionment testing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (assessable income less allowable deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil for a qualifying offshore IC; any positive figure here triggers the flat 27% rate notwithstanding the IC's offshore status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at the flat 27% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Multiply Line 11 by 27%; a zero Line 11 yields a zero tax entry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits: foreign tax credits, imputation credits, and installment prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax is creditable only if the same income is also assessed as Samoan-source; a nil-assessable IC will not generally use this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount payable to the MoR or amount to be refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expected nil in the tax-exempt IC model; a refund claim requires a valid Tax Residency Certificate and supporting DTA documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late IR2 filing triggers a failure-to-furnish penalty of WS$1,000 plus a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax assessed for the first month of default and 2% for each subsequent month, capped at 25% of total tax. Unpaid corporate tax bears statutory interest at 1.5% per month (18% per annum), compounded daily; the Commissioner may issue an asset-based default assessment without further notice and may issue a Departure Prohibition Order against directors for deliberate non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% — the statutory dividend withholding tax rate imposed under the Income Tax Act 2015 on dividends distributed by a Samoan company to a non-resident shareholder. Dividends paid by a tax-exempt International Company solely out of foreign-source income to a non-resident shareholder are outside the Samoan income tax base and therefore carry an effective 0% withholding tax rate; no formal WHT clearance is required for such distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a Double Taxation Agreement applies (principal operative treaties: Samoa–New Zealand; Samoa has also entered DTA arrangements with Australia, Norway, Sweden, and Finland), the recipient must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the treaty partner's competent authority; (ii) deliver the TRC and a completed Treaty Relief Claim Notification to the paying IC's registered agent before the distribution date; (iii) ensure the IC submits the related WHT schedules to the MoR together with the IR2 filing; and (iv) if the full 15% rate was withheld in the absence of the TRC, lodge a refund application with the MoR within 3 years of the withholding event, attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers, and an identity-confirmation affidavit. Treaty-shopping through an IC that lacks beneficial ownership of the dividend will be rejected under the Principal Purpose Test. For PRC-resident holders of a Samoan IC where no bilateral DTA with Samoa is in force, treaty relief is unavailable and the full statutory 15% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 15% on royalties (including software licensing, game-asset licensing, and IP licensing fees) and 15% on interest paid to non-residents under the Income Tax Act 2015. Under operative Samoan DTAs, the rates are typically reduced to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, with select treaty protocols providing 5% for bank interest on loans to financial institutions. Classification of 3D art fees as royalties versus business profits depends on whether the transaction transfers a license of copyrighted art assets (royalty) or constitutes a supply of personal services (business profits, taxable in Samoa only if attributable to a permanent establishment).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 10,000,000 — Samoa's transfer pricing rules follow the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. A Local File is administratively required where the value of controlled transactions with a single related enterprise exceeds WST 1,000,000, and a Master File where aggregate cross-border related-party turnover exceeds WST 10,000,000 in a fiscal year. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is recommended for all IC invoicing to related foreign gaming studios because the MoR may benchmark the service margin under TNMM and impute Samoan-source profits if the IC is re-characterized as tax-resident.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations, operative from 1 January 2020, apply to every IC carrying on a relevant activity. A 3D art outsourcing studio classified under ISIC 7490 may fall within the 'service center', 'headquarters', or 'intellectual property business' categories. Such ICs must demonstrate: (i) core income-generating activities directed toward foreign game clients at least supervised from Samoa; (ii) adequate physical premises, full-time employees, and operating expenditure proportionate to the scale of offshore activity; and (iii) an annual economic substance notification filed through SIFSA. Failure to satisfy the substance test results in loss of the tax exemption and application of the penalties detailed below.
